detail: `search` mangles the first/last token of a query via sanitize_fts5_query step 4 (src/persistence/stock_sqlite.rs:1079-1092): the dangling-operator stripper uses string starts_with/ends_with instead of whole-token matching, so 'notes'->'es', 'nothing'->'hing', 'notable'->'able', 'android'->'roid', 'order'->'der', 'oracle'->'acle', 'command'->'comm', 'brand'->'br', 'band'->'b', 'the command'->'the comm'. The store then returns hits=0 for text that IS present, with no error, so a user cannot tell a mangled query from a genuine miss. Hit while driving the published boundary as a real Python consumer over a 4,000-message archive: 9 of 16 ordinary words probe as SILENT MISS (adapter 0 vs the same file's own messages_fts MATCH 1) — docs/evidence/dogfood-20261017/opbug.log. Wrong-answer demo (wrong-answer.log): one row holds 'bra measurements only' and one holds 'brand measurements only'; `search "brand"` returns 0 rows while messages_fts MATCH 'brand' returns the brand row (rowid 2). Bisect at the SQL level in bisect-search.log. Fix direction: compare WHOLE tokens (split_whitespace + eq_ignore_ascii_case) before dropping a dangling AND/OR/NOT, or drop step 4 entirely (FTS5 tolerates the operators), and add one regression case per word in the probe table.

Before: 'brand'→'br', 'notes'→'es', 'nothing'→'hing'. After: correct token-level matching preserves operator-dropping only for complete tokens. detail: sanitize step 2 deletes the FTS5-special set (src/persistence/stock_sqlite.rs:1049-1054) with NO separator, so adjacent words merge into a token that exists nowhere ('src/main.rs'->'srcmain.rs', 'cost=5.50'->'cost5.50', 'slash/x'->'slashx', 'path C:\\Users\\kara'->'path CUserskara'), and step 5 (:1093-1120) then quotes the merged token as a phrase. Result: 19 of 31 realistic verbatim strings a user can SEE in their own transcript (file paths, cost= values, emails, punctuation) return 0 hits although the stdlib sqlite3 LIKE finds the literal in the same row (docs/evidence/dogfood-20261017/search-fidelity.log). The zero is silent: 'zzz-no-such-text-zzz' and 'zzz/no-such/text' also return 0, and the non-stale path has no LIKE fallback (like_fallback at stock_sqlite.rs:1342 serves only the stale/corrupt arms) and no diagnostic, so a user cannot distinguish 'no matches' from 'your query was rewritten'. Fix direction: substitute a space for the specials instead of deleting them (keep token boundaries), and when the sanitized query yields 0 hits while the RAW term is present in canonical rows, answer from the LIKE arm or return a machine-visible 'query rewritten' signal.

detail: specs/python-interop.md §3.1 states the store exposes "exactly the §6.1 operation set (ensure_session, append_message, get_messages, search_messages, end_session, record_model_usage)"; persistence-shim.md §6.1 additionally lists append_messages_batch ('one transaction for the whole batch'). Reality at HEAD 887a257: `grep -rn append_messages_batch src/` = 1 hit, a doc comment; BatchAppendReport (api.rs:426) has no producer and no consumer (only the mod.rs re-export); WriteTxn record_model_usage is declared (api.rs:483) and implemented stock_sqlite.rs:822, but the adapter dispatch (session_adapter.rs:133-340) exposes only hello/ping/open/ensure_session/append_message/get_messages/get_session/end_session/search/checkpoint/backup/close/shutdown — so a Python consumer can neither batch a transcript nor record model usage. Cost of the missing batch path, measured as the consumer: 2,000 messages through the boundary = 19.48s (103 msg/s, one durable commit per message) vs 0.048s (41,270 msg/s) for the same bytes in ONE transaction via stdlib sqlite3 = 402x (bulk-ab.log); the 4,000-message archive leg took 29.5s (136 msg/s). Per single append this is 7-10ms — imperceptible — so the finding is the MISSING BATCH surface, not a slow append. Fix direction: implement append_messages_batch in the slice and expose append_messages_batch + record_model_usage on the wire, or correct §3.1 to name the exposed subset explicitly.
title: Dogfood: §6.1 append_messages_batch has no implementation and record_model_usage is unreachable over the wire (§3.1 claims the whole §6.1 set) — bulk import pays 402x

detail: Fresh-install leg on ephemeral bunker agent hrs-df-1017 (server bunker-mvp, 2026-10-17, HEAD 887a257, bare Debian user, no sudo): clone of the documented public origin 1s; rustup installed exactly as README points (https://rustup.rs) 16s -> cargo 1.99.1; documented `cargo build` rc=0 in 25s; then the README's own smoke verb `cargo test` returned rc=101: "test result: FAILED. 17 passed; 5 failed" in tests/hrs010_session_store.rs — f2_rust_write_then_sqlite3_reads_the_same_file (:259), slice_record_model_usage_upserts_and_falls_back_to_session_route (:653), f9_generation_counter_increments_and_never_decrements (:579), migration_newer_schema_version_is_refused_not_downgraded (:681), stale_fts_marker_serves_canonical_rows_not_partial_search (:982) — every one panicking with Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound } because the test shells out to a `sqlite3` CLI the fresh box does not have, with no preflight and no recorded skip. Control: the SAME commit on the control host (sqlite3 3.53.4 present) is 29/29 green across all 9 test binaries, so the class is machine-dependent — but the documented clean-checkout path still ends red for a fresh user, and README Development says only 'From a clean checkout, run: cargo build; cargo test' (no prerequisite named). The headline feature DOES work on that box: the HRS-003 e2e proof passed all five markers with the adapter built there (bunker-e2e.log: ROUNDTRIP_OK / SQLITE3_REOPEN_OK / SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION=31 / ERROR_STRUCTURED / LIFECYCLE_CLEAN). Fix direction: preflight the CLI in those 5 tests and record a capability SKIP with the reason (repo doctrine: recorded skips, never silent), or do the read-back through the bundled SQLite via Rust instead of the CLI, and name any remaining prerequisite in README Development. Same env class DF-HRS-103 adjudicated as harness (chaos-resource); this run shows it also breaks the project's own documented install smoke. DF-HRS-101 ('no install path to prove') is superseded by this run: an install path now exists and was exercised end-to-end.

detail: tests/hrs003_python_interop.rs:23 writes the checked-in evidence file docs/evidence/hrs003/broken-case-transcript.txt on EVERY test run (the non-vacuity leg runs the driver's --mode broken), and the file embeds a wall-clock Date line plus the per-run temp adapter path. Observed for real: after a clean `cargo test --workspace` (rc=0, 29 passed) the working tree was dirty with exactly that file, diff = 2 lines (Date: 2026-10-16T14:09:43Z -> 2026-10-17T14:47:00Z; Adapter binary /var/tmp/hermes-scratch/hrs003-adapter-broken-1618961 -> ...-1527313) — and the file was ALREADY dirty when this dogfood tick started, so every lane that runs the suite leaves the same dirt for the next one. It has already cost the repo one CI cycle: commit d3877a8 'strip blank line at EOF in DF-HRS-103 control-host proof log (CI whitespace gate)'. Consequences: `git status` can never be clean on a host that ran the suite, unrelated commits capture the churn if a lane commits by wildcard, and CI gates on whitespace keep firing on a regenerated artifact. Fix direction: keep the tracked file as a recorded artifact but have the test write only on a substantive change (compare before writing), or write the transcript to a temp path and assert on it there, leaving the committed copy as the checked-in reference; then un-dirty the working tree in CI.
